Elma's reconnoitering of Alrest is a series of tasks given through 's requirements. Through these tasks, Elma sees some of the sights of Alrest, while discussing some of its similarities and differences with Mira with some of the party members. As such, for a scene to be available, Elma must be in the party along with the characters specified on the corresponding Affinity Chart node's requirements. Viewing a scene will unlock the corresponding level of Keen Eye and reveal the requirements for the and nodes of the same level. The scenes must be viewed in order, meaning that for a certain level of Keen Eye to be revealed, all Keen Eye nodes of a lower level must be unlocked.

Element orbs are a battle mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and Torna ~ The Golden Country. They are conceptual objects "attached" to enemies as a result of using Blade Combos. The used in the combo determines which element of orb is attached. Only one orb of each element can be on a foe at a time, meaning the max is eight (one of each). Under normal circumstances, an orb is only created by the final step of a level 3 Blade Combo, so a single orb requires at least three s to be used. If the 's Orb Master or 100-Series System Battle Skill activates, or the game is Torna ~ The Golden Country, any Special will add an orb regardless of the Blade Combo level. Enemy Arts are the s used by enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles and Future Connected. Like party members, enemies can have up to 8 different Arts that they may use in battle, in addition to auto-attacks. Some Arts are shared by several enemies, while others are exclusive to individuals. The primary difference between enemy Arts and party member Arts is that enemy Arts require a period of windup, typically one second, for which the enemy must stay still in a charging animation. For the song see Encyclopedia (music). The Encyclopedia () is a feature in Xenosaga Freaks. It features entries about topics from Xenosaga Episode I. They are different from the database entries in Xenosaga Episode I, Xenosaga Episode III and Xenosaga I & II. Not all articles are unlocked from the start, some are tied to conditions in Xeno-comi, Xeno-pittan and the Xenosaga Episode II Demo. All articles feature a title and a headline. Articles may also include a thumbnail, an extra image, a video clip, a voice sample, and links to other articles. They are split into four different categories: Characters (), World (), Products (), and Keywords ().

Estham () is a location mentioned a few times in Torna ~ The Golden Country. It is first brought up by Mikhail, who claims to have been sold from there to Porton Village. It is implied by Martha to be a Titan, and Fred states that Estham was attacked in a similar manner to Feltley Village not long ago. Much like Coeia, Estham's existence is never acknowledged in the main game. While Estham is implied to be its own Titan by NPC dialogues, a chat between Mikhail and Milton, after the party arrives at Yanchik Harbor, implies that the former never took a Titan ship before, which seems to contradict that Estham is separate from Torna.

Ether Defence Up is a buff in Xenoblade Chronicles. It raises the user's ether defence, thus reducing damage taken from ether attacks. Whether Physical Defence Up is better than is a complex matter that depends on many factors. Generally, because Ether Defense Up is a percentage-based boost to the user's defence, it will be ineffective if the user's defence is low to start with. This buff does not have an explanation associated with it, perhaps because there is no art that applies it by itself.

Expert Mode is a gameplay option in Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition and Future Connected. Contrary to what the name might imply, it is not a "hard mode", and has no effects in battle at all. Instead, it provides a means to avoid over-levelling, thus allowing the player to do as many quests and other side content as desired without having to worry about combat becoming trivially easy. It can also be used to intentionally under-level for challenge runs or similar. When enabled, Expert Mode has two main effects. * EXP gained from completing s, discovering s and s, and earning s is not applied to characters immediately. Instead, it is stored aside for use later. Fields are a mechanic in Xenoblade Chronicles 3 and Future Redeemed in which certain s place a circle on the ground that applies an effect to participants that position within it. Most fields provide healing or buffs to the setter and their allies, while some instead cause damage or debuffs to opponents. The party may only have 3 fields active at a time; having the Ring à la Mode will increase this to 4. Placing another will cause the field with the lowest remaining duration to go out with a bang - damage and healing fields will do an extra-large dose, while buff and debuff fields will apply a regular version of their buff/debuff, thus compensating for not reaching its full duration.
